title: Cash-strapped De Montfort University could sell off more buildings
excerpt: Bosses are understood to be weighing up the future of three more sites
content:
Cash-strapped De Montfort University could sell off more buildings to tackle budget black hole

Bosses are understood to be weighing up the future of three more sites

06:00, 02 Nov 2026

Cash-strapped De Montfort University (DMU) is considering selling more buildings in Leicester as it grapples with an £8m budget black hole.

The future of three key sites, Edith Murphy House, Heritage House and Bede House, is now up in the air as bosses weigh up potential sales or lettings.

It follows DMU's confirmation earlier this year that it was actively considering options to vacate, sell, or externally lease several key sites, specifically naming its Bede Island campus and the Leicester Media School.

At the time, university chiefs said they were having to “think differently” about how DMU operates to ensure its estate is “efficient and right-sized”.

‌

Now, LeicestershireLive understands that talks over potential sales or lettings have expanded to include three further major sites.

Edith Murphy House and Heritage House, both on Southgates, and Bede House, in Western Boulevard, are currently home to key operations including library services, finance and IT, as well as part of the Faculty of Health and Life Sciences.

The university previously blamed its financial pressures on government changes to UK Visas and Immigration practice, which it warned would “severely restrict our ability to recruit overseas students from some countries”.

‌

An internal letter sent to staff in May warned of “significant shortfalls that will require further action” once it saw how many students arrived in the autumn.

When asked for comment on the future of Edith Murphy House, Heritage House and Bede House, a DMU spokesperson did not confirm or deny that the buildings were part of discussions, but stated that the university had no confirmed updates.

They said DMU was managing all of its resources through its updated strategy to meet the financial challenges facing universities.

‌

Alongside assessing its estate, the university has opened a voluntary severance scheme, inviting staff to submit expressions of interest in leaving.
